newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude flat with slow spot WTI trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude flat with slow spot WTI trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude oil prices were little changed Tuesday, in line with a flat West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) market, traders said.
No deals were reported and dealing for West Coast crudes remained thin Tuesday.

Local sales of light grade Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude -- the regional benchmark -- remained was flat, with interest weak as several West Coast refiners continue to deal with poor margins by cutting runs.
Exxon sold a cargo of ANS to Shell Oil Monday, traders said, but the deal was negotiated on secret "formula" terms, which allow parties to establish a price based on a monthly average of prices.
Key seller BP continued to offer at $1.85 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI), but saw no buyers.

Discounts for ANS remained $2.16 a barrel under WTI. With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude rose to $17.01/17.16 a barrel, a mere one cent higher than Monday. The basis of ANS, the spot market, saw little movement today ahead of the WTI August contract expiry.
Meanwhile, Kern River grade remained 10 to 20 cents over postings. Wilmington crude, pumped from Long Beach, Calif., stood 65 to 75 cents over posting, unchanged for over a month.
Line 63 crude remained unchanged at $3.05 under WTI and about $1.00 over Buena Vista crude.
West Crude traders dismissed the 1.4 million barrel build in West Coast crude stocks.
